picks.catalyst: Gap down: earnings beat, but CEO stepping down and full-year guidance only reaffirmed
picks.why: Nutanix beat on its quarter, but said CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down once a successor is found and kept its full-year sales target (midpoint below estimates), so it's down about 12%; a CEO change hurts sentiment more than the business, which is the kind of gap down that can bounce once early sellers are done.

picks.catalyst: Gap down despite record quarter and raised full-year outlook (AI chip sell-off)
picks.why: Dell posted record quarterly revenue of $54.9B, beat on profit ($9.45 vs $6.59 expected) and raised its full-year sales outlook to $202B, yet it's down in pre-market (reports range from about 3% to 6%) because AI and chip stocks are selling off; the business news is good, so this is a sentiment dip that can reverse, but the sector is weak, so check the live quote and respect the stop.

picks.catalyst: Gap down: earnings beat, but next-quarter subscription forecast slightly light
picks.why: Workday beat on profit ($2.82 vs $2.75) and sales and even raised its full-year subscription and margin targets, but its next-quarter subscription forecast ($2.6B) came in just under the $2.61B expected, so it's down about 10%; that's a small guidance trim on a big, liquid name, which can set up a bounce.

Li Auto reported better-than-expected third-quarter results, with sales of $4.30B vs $4.09B expected, so it's up about 5% while most of the market is red; a real beat gives buyers a reason to step in, but it's a cheaper stock close to the $10 floor, so keep size small.
